summary: Configured inventory-worker on node1 as inventorysvc in a root-owned chroot. Only /var/lib/inventory is application-writable. SELinux remains enforcing, OS/kernel/packages were preserved, and the service recovered after both process termination and a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Created the non-login system account inventorysvc (UID/GID 992).
Built a minimal root-owned chroot using the installed Bash runtime; no packages were installed or upgraded.
Installed and enabled inventory-worker.service with RootDirectory, strict filesystem protection, no capabilities, and no-new-privileges.
Configured persistent SELinux file contexts compatible with the copied runtime.
Tested allowed writes, denied writes, hidden host files, advancing worker output, and automatic worker restart.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and all required service, data, security, and access checks recovered.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated unprivileged inventorysvc account and root-owned chroot
evidence.summary: Shows UID/GID 992, nologin account, root-owned mode-0755 chroot, matching live process-root inode, and the worker running under UID/GID 992.
Writable-directory audits identify only /var/lib/inventory; protected writes are denied, application writes succeed, temporary tests are removed, and host /etc/os-release is hidden.

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker is managed, persistent, and automatically recovers
evidence.summary: Systemd replaced a terminated worker with a new PID, the heartbeat recovered, and the enabled service started automatically after node reboot.

evidence.requirement: OS, kernel, security controls, listeners, and administrative access preserved
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1 remain unchanged; SELinux is enforcing, SSH is active with unchanged configuration checksum, listeners are unchanged, and no failed units remain.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart and recovery sequence
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 21972395-6444-42bf-8e37-5c3108194a7d was captured, safe reboot acknowledged, new boot ID 90774ef3-04e0-40b1-83ab-5901550ed202 observed, and post-restart service, heartbeat, confinement, data access, SSH, SELinux, and integrity checks passed.
